newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil concerned about trade gap with U.S.-report.
newsitem.headline: Brazil concerned about trade gap with U.S.-report.

text.p: The Brazilian government is concerned about the country's $1.6 billion trade gap with the United States and has asked its embassy in Washington to closely monitor the imbalance, a local newspaper said.
Gazeta Mercantil, quoting embassy officials in Washington, said President Fernando Henrique Cardoso's government is concerned about high tariffs imposed on Brazilian orange juice.

It also is worried about rising tariffs on leather, shoes, textiles, clothing, beverages, tobacco, non-metallic minerals and petrochemical products as well as Washington's method for calculating anti-dumping and compensation on steel exports.
The paper said Ambassador Paulo Tarso Flecha de Lima has been asked to follow with concern these "irritating factors" in bilateral trade.
Gazeta quoted Flecha de Lima as saying the embassy in Washington had recommended Brasilia file a complaint with the World Trade Organization over U.S.'s anti-dumping legislation.
Brazilian Foreign Minister Luiz Felipe Lampreia is slated to travel to Washington on Thursday to review bilateral trade relations, the paper said.
